'''Chandan Dasgupta''' ({{langx|bn|চন্দন দাশগুপ্ত}}), (born 1951) is an Indian [[theoretical physicist]] known for his contributions in [[condensed matter physics]] and [[statistical physics]]. He is at present a professor at [[Indian Institute of Science]], Bangalore.<ref name="Prof Chandan Dasgupta's homepage at IISc Physics website">{{cite web | url=http://www.physics.iisc.ernet.in/~cdgupta/ | title=Prof Chandan Dasgupta's homepage at IISc Physics website | accessdate=9 March 2014}}</ref><ref name="Prof Chandan Dasgupta's page at ICTS website">{{cite web | url=http://www.icts.res.in/people/1/details/88/ | title=Prof Chandan Dasgupta's page at ICTS website | accessdate=9 March 2014}}</ref><ref name="Prof Chandan Dasgupta- Fellow of Indian National Science Academy">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.org/detail.php?id=P00-1273 | title=Prof Chandan Dasgupta- Fellow of Indian National Science Academy | accessdate=9 March 2014 | url-status=dead | archiveurl=https://archive.today/20140309094539/http://insaindia.org/detail.php?id=P00-1273 | archivedate=9 March 2014 }}</ref> He was the former<ref name="Indian Institute of Science Administration Deans">{{cite web | url=http://www.iisc.ernet.in/administration/deans.php | title=Indian Institute of Science Administration Deans | accessdate=10 August 2015}}</ref> dean of Undergraduate Program at [[Indian Institute of Science]].<ref name="Drawing India's Brightest to the Cause of Science, Hindustan Times">{{cite news | url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/delhi-news/drawing-india-s-brightest-to-the-cause-of-science/story-8BpzsuyWD2cBcLEJMHb0QM.html | title=Drawing India's Brightest to the Cause of Science | date=5 January 2013 | first=Charu Sudan | last=Kasturi | newspaper=Hindustan Times | accessdate=10 March 2014}}</ref>

==Biography==
Chandan Dasgupta earned his BSc degree in 1971 from [[Presidency College, Kolkata|Presidency College]], [[University of Calcutta]] and MSc degree from [[Delhi University]] in 1973. He did his doctoral research at the [[University of Pennsylvania]], USA under the supervision of Professor AB Harris and obtained PhD degree in Physics in 1978. Subsequently, he did post-doctoral research at the [[University of California, San Diego]] with Shang-keng Ma <ref name=" Low-temperature properties of the random Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain, Phys. Rev. B 22, 1305">{{cite journal | title=Low-temperature properties of the random Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain | doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.22.1305 | year=1980 | last1=Dasgupta | first1=Chandan | last2=Ma | first2=Shang-Keng | journal=Physical Review B | volume=22 | issue=3 | pages=1305–1319 }}</ref> and at [[Harvard University]] with [[Bertrand Halperin]], and worked as a faculty member in the School of Physics and Astronomy of the [[University of Minnesota]] for a few years. He joined the Indian Institute of Science in 1987, where, at present, he is a Professor.

Professor Dasgupta played a major role in the establishment of the Centre for Condensed Matter Theory at the Indian Institute of Science in 1998 and acted as the Convenor of the Centre (1998-2005). He is an Honorary Professor at the [[Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research]]<ref name="Condensed Matter Theory at JNCASR">{{cite web | url=http://www.jncasr.ac.in/cmtumain.php/Faculty-members/1/1/ | title=Condensed Matter Theory at JNCASR | accessdate=8 April 2014}}</ref> and holds a Visiting Professorship at the [[University of Minnesota]], USA.

==Research==
Prof Chandan Dasgupta's area of specialization is theoretical condensed matter physics with emphasis on statistical mechanics.
* Supercooled liquids and the [[glass transition]]<ref name="Growing length and time scales in glass-forming liquids, 3675–3679, doi: 10.1073/pnas.0811082106">{{cite journal | title=Growing length and time scales in glass-forming liquids | journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences | date=10 March 2009 | volume=106 | issue=10 | pages=3675–3679 | last1=Karmakar | first1=Smarajit | last2=Dasgupta | first2=Chandan | last3=Sastry | first3=Srikanth | doi=10.1073/pnas.0811082106 | pmid=19234111 | pmc=2656139 | doi-access=free }}</ref>
* [[Superconductivity]] and [[superfluidity]]<ref name=" Phase Transition in a Lattice Model of Superconductivity, Phys. Rev. Lett. 47, 1556">{{cite journal | title=Phase Transition in a Lattice Model of Superconductivity | doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.47.1556 | year=1981 | last1=Dasgupta | first1=C. | last2=Halperin | first2=B. I. | journal=Physical Review Letters | volume=47 | issue=21 | pages=1556–1560 }}</ref>
* Dynamics of nonequilibrium systems
* Physics at the nanoscale

==Awards and honours==
Chandan Dasgupta was awarded Sir C.V. Raman Award for Research in Physical Sciences in 2006 by the [[University Grants Commission (India)|University Grants Commission]].<ref name="Honours & Awards, UGC website">{{cite web | url=http://www.ugc.ac.in/page/honours-and-awards.aspx | title=Honours & Awards, UGC website | accessdate=10 March 2014}}</ref>
In 2007, he was elected as a fellow of [[TWAS|The World Academy of Sciences]] .<ref name="Chandan Dasgupta, Elected fellow of TWAS">{{cite web | url=http://www.twas.org/member/dasgupta-chandan | title=Chandan Dasgupta, Elected fellow of TWAS | accessdate=16 May 2014}}</ref>
He was awarded with "The Satyendranath Bose Medal" by [[Indian National Science Academy]] in 2018.<ref name="CDG SNBoseINSA">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#12 | title=Recipients of Medals/Lectures Awards | accessdate=29 June 2018 | archive-date=16 September 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916233840/http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#12 | url-status=dead }}</ref>
